pr_body:
Fixes #46031 

See "log redaction" RFC from #48076 for details.

General concept:

- logs stored on disk contain markers around data items potentially
  containing PII or confidential data (“unsafe data”).

- `debug zip`, `debug merge-log`, and the `Logs` and `LogFiles` RPCs
  edit the log entries upon request to replace all the unsafe data by
  `‹×›`.

See also the release notes below for a summary of UX.

Release note (cli change): Certain kinds of advanced troubleshooting
information, for example internal details from the Go runtime, are now
output to a separate log file in the configured log directory.  This
file is named `<program>-stderr.xxx.log`.

Release note (cli change): The server CLI commands (`start`,
`start-single-node`, `demo`) now support a new flag
`--redactable-logs`, which introduces markers in generated log entries
to facilitate redaction of sensitive information by `cockroach debug
zip` and other CockroachDB APIs. This flag is currently not enabled by
default, but is recommended for all deployments and will be enabled by
default in a later version.

This feature is experimental.

Note: the flag is *advertised* (in `--help`) by `cockroach start` and
`cockroach start-single-node`, where log files are expected as a
matter of course; it is also supported, yet *hidden* (from `--help`),
by every other CLI command because every command can also produce log
entries when passed `--log-dir` or `--logtostderr`.

Release note (cli change): The commands `cockroach debug zip` and
`cockroach debug merge-logs` support a new flag `--redact-logs`. When
specified, it causes log messages that potentially contain
confidential data or PII to be redacted away.

This feature is experimental.

Note 1: At the time of this writing, this redaction is extremely
aggressive and may hinder the ability of Cockroach Labs to investigate
issues from log files, especially if `--redactable-logs` is not
enabled server-side.

Note 2: Other potentially-confidential data may still be retrieved by
`cockroach debug zip`; the new flag only applies to retrieved log
files inside the output zip file.

I haven't looked at the change in detail, but the redacted output looks like it should be redacting keys from log tags which it is not currently doing:

```
I200426 20:06:49.615435 524 kv/kvserver/replica_consistency.go:255  [n1,consistencyChecker,s1,r4/1:/System{/tsd-tse}] triggering stats recomputation to resolve delta of <REDACTED>
```

Specifically, the `/System{/tsd-tse}` part of the log tag can contain table keys. Is this something you're planning to address in a subsequent PR?

> Specifically, the /System{/tsd-tse} part of the log tag can contain table keys. Is this something you're planning to address in a subsequent PR?

I already called it out in the commit message as "left over work" that needs to be addressed in this PR before it even merges.

I put the PR out to stimulate discussion this week about the approach. I'm not keen on advancing in this direction if the discussion steers me somewhere else.

> The markers are selected to be no-op on standard unix terminals.

But not in `less`, `emacs`, or `vim` (where they appear as `^N` and `^O`). 

> logs need preprocessing to be greppable

What do you mean? I just made a test file and it works for me. But losing easy greppability seems like a significant downside.


I'm not a fan of digging up obscure characters that seem to be unused (and invisible!) in practice and giving them new meanings. This seems likely to bite us somehow. (For example, as part of a convoluted security vulnerability, inserting `^O` characters into someone's database might be a way to defeat their log redactions).

We have occasional requests for changes to our log format (e.g. https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/44755), which is non-standard (and kind of annoying even when you're used to it - that leading `IWEF` character was a bad choice). Maybe it's time to introduce a second log stream in a structured format (which would make pre-processing effectively mandatory) from which the redacted and unredacted logs could be generated. We could continue logging the current format for a time as well.

I'm preparing a RFC, this will be a better place for a discussion.

Misc feedback:

> But not in less, emacs, or vim (where they appear as ^N and ^O).

`less -r` works. For emacs/vim, that's easy to solve with editor configurations.

> > logs need preprocessing to be greppable
> What do you mean?

Most of the text is still greppable (that was a big motivation for this particular approach!!), but you need to be careful about text that straddles a marker boundary.

> (For example, as part of a convoluted security vulnerability, inserting ^O characters into someone's database might be a way to defeat their log redactions).

I've thought about this, they will be escaped appropriately.

> Maybe it's time to introduce a second log stream in a structured format which would make pre-processing effectively mandatory

That is indeed planned, but I consider this to be orthogonal. Moreover, the mandatory pre-processing does not bring us in a better place than the proposal here.
RFC at #48076

I think this now does what is said in #48076 so ready for review.

Heads up that there's an unforeseen small roadblock: we have historically redirected stderr (file descriptor 2) to go to the log file, because the Go runtime is print-happy whenever it detects something is amiss, and fd2 is hardcoded in the Go runtime sources. Example uses:

- panic message + traceback upon crashes
- detected heap corruptions
- unexpected signals
- out of memory
- stack depth exceeded

etc

Now, there's so much potentially printed in there that we cannot assume all of it is safe. Additionally, anything printed by the Go runtime into a CockroachDB log files *makes that output logically part of the last log entry printed*, **because we don't have terminating delimiters for log entries.**

I have tried to spawn a goroutine internally that uses `os.Pipe` to provision fd2, and adds redaction annotation to everything printed there. Unfortunately, when the Go runtime is unhappy, that goroutine is not given a chance to run (or not on time) and we lose the output.

I am seeing two ways forward here; either:

1. **stop redirecting fd2** to the crdb log file;
2. **introduce a terminating delimiter for log entries**, that would be inserted at the end of the log entry whenever the entry is redactable. Then we'd make the entry reader/parser ignore everything after the delimiter and before the start of the next valid entry.

The advantage of (2) is that it keeps the runtime messages in the log files as previously. However it adds even more markers into the logging output. Also, more concerning, **writes to fd2 by the runtime and the log file by `log` could be interleaved**, causing the unsafe runtime output to appear "inside" a log entry.

This makes my preference go to (1), which has the advantage of being safe without additional implementation complexity, and without the risk that further changes would introduce leaks mistakenly.

We could stop redirecting fd2 completely, and then tell users "give us your stderr output whenever you contact support". Or we could instead redirect it to a separate "stderr output file" in the log directory, which would be gathered separately by `debug zip`, not gathered when redaction is enabled, and not visible to the log file retrieval RPC.

Thoughts?

Hmm, that's unfortunate. I agree that option 2) seems untenable. I agree
that we should go forward with option 1), though it would be a bummer to
lose the stack traces when redaction is on. `panicparse`[1] will let us
safely recover any stack traces and we can probably also get the relevant
information from the `panic: ` line if there is one. It's work, but not too
bad.

[1]: https://github.com/maruel/panicparse

We'll get the stack traces for panic, that's not an issue. We get them because the stopper ensures the stacks are printed to logs (and sent to sentry) when a task finishes with a panic.

The main issue is all the non-stacktrace details, for example heap corruptions etc.

> We could stop redirecting fd2 completely, and then tell users "give us your stderr output whenever you contact support". Or we could instead redirect it to a separate "stderr output file" in the log directory, which would be gathered separately by debug zip, not gathered when redaction is enabled, and not visible to the log file retrieval RPC.

I think we need to use a separate stderr file in the log directory. It's not tenable to ask users to save stderr and be able to give it to us on request; the difficulty of doing that in practice across the diversity of deployment environments is why we implemented the (hacky) fd2 redirection in the first place. 

It's unfortunate to lose these files completely when redacting. I don't know how often we end up getting useful information here, but I think it's rare for them to contain sensitive information. We may want to have an option to collect stderr files without unredacting all the rest (maybe showing them to the user for inspection.

> We may want to have an option to collect stderr files without unredacting all the rest (maybe showing them to the user for inspection.

yes agreed. I'll try to cook something up towards that.

I found an elegant solution: keep the stderr redirect to a regular log file, but use a secondary logger. Then make the "reportable" flag (and thus the vertical ellipsis marker) per-logger, and disable it from the stderr log file.

This way the stderr output remains naturally visible via the RPCs and `debug zip`
the stderr redirection stuff works fine. I'll wrap this up soon.

I'll process any further feedback in followup PRs.

issue_context.title: cli: support `debug zip --anonymize`
issue_context.body:
We should provide this switch so that diagnosing of issues is not hindered by manual scrubbing by the user -- which could be prone to mistakes as well.

Few examples:
-  The table/key names (XXXX) in log lines:
```
I200311 07:21:32.053215 826880069 storage/replica_command.go:797 [n8,replicate,s8,r16277/42:/Table/131{-/1/"XXXX…}] change replicas (REMOVE_REPLICA (n5,s5):37): read existing descriptor r16277:/Table/131{-/1/"XXXX^51b23f4c1607fe220acebc023621568f"} [(n4,s4):40, (n8,s8):42, (n5,s5):37, (n11,s11):43, next=44, gen=8]
```
- The same as above in range reports, rangelog.json
- User names used to log into the admin UI
comments:
@irfansharif Just want to +1 this issue. I've been asked to provide a debug zip a few times now but due to restrictions have to make sure I scrub all PII from the dump. Currently I got some crazy `sed` commands to deal with this but having an `anonymize` flag as proposed here would me sleep a little bit better :smile: 

I see there's already a PR ongoing for it, if you'd like I'm happy to pitch in :+1:
I empathize with your pain! Hopefully there's not much of that before long. There's a bit of design work ongoing by @knz over at #48076, that you may be interested in.
